newsitem.title: UK: Fisher sets P&O tanker buy, rights.
newsitem.headline: Fisher sets P&O tanker buy, rights.

text.p: Small British shipping group James Fisher and Sons Plc said on Wednesday it had conditionally agreed to buy a petroleum product tanker operating company from transport and property giant P&O, for 19.2 million stg cash and the assumption of various debt and other obligations.

Fisher said it intended to help finance the proposed deal with a one-for-one rights issue of 24 million shares at 120p per share, and that pending approval of the plans from its shareholders it had temporarily suspended its shares.

Fisher said the planned acquisition, which fits in with Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co's strategy of disposing of non-core assets, would add revenue at the same time as allowing proportionately lower overheads.
The ships, which carry so-called clean petroleum products around Britain and Europe, will be combined with Fisher's existing fleet of similar vessels.

Included in the purchase contract are agreements to take delivery of four 3,700 dwt tankers ordered by P&O at Shanghai's Qiu Xin shipyard for an estimated total cost of $46.5 million. Fisher expects to take on about 16.8 million stg of this debt.
In terms of net fixed assets, the deal will more than double the size of James Fisher's group to 56.68 million stg compared with 27.45 million stg at June 30 this year.
Its longer term debts will also rise sharply, giving it an overall balance of net assets of 37.13 million pounds, up from 21.53 million at June 30.

"The 17 ships currently operated by P&O Tankships together with the six new ships that the enlarged group now has on order will make James Fisher the leader in British and Irish transportation of clean petroleum products and a significant participant in the European market," David Cobb, Fisher's executive chairman, said in the statement.

As part of the rights issue proposals, the company said it would expect to make a pretax profit in the current calendar year of not less than 4.9 million stg and expects to recommend a final dividend of 1.5p, giving a total year dividend of 2.5p. Newly-issued shares would also qualify for this final payout.
The company expects to raise about 27.4 million stg net through the rights issue.
P&O will also receive warrants to subscribe for one million shares at a 175p excercise price between November 1997 and 2001.
